text:
No, the statement is false.

The claim that the Great Wall is visible to the naked eye from space (including low Earth orbit) is a longstanding myth. It is too narrow, follows terrain that camouflages it, and lacks sufficient contrast with the surrounding landscape to be reliably distinguished by unaided human vision from orbital altitudes. Astronaut reports, photographic analysis, and statements from space agencies (including NASA and accounts by Chinese taikonauts) consistently confirm this. Many other human-made features (cities, highways, airports, large mines, etc.) are far easier to see. Visibility claims usually involve telephoto imagery, ideal lighting/atmospheric conditions, or confusion with other linear features.
